diagnostic_approaches.name: Radiographic size-based malignancy risk estimation for pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Estimate malignancy risk based on nodule size on CT
criteria_or_scoring: Probability of malignancy for nodules <6 mm around 1%
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Take into consideration size, density, location, edge characteristics, calcification, and changes between serial scans.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Smaller nodules are more likely to be benign.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Initial radiographic assessment to guide malignancy risk.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Smaller nodules are more likely to be benign, with the probability of malignancy for nodules <6 mm around 1%, and for those 6–8 mm between 1% and 2%

diagnostic_approaches.name: Volume doubling time (VDT) assessment on serial imaging
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate benign from malignant nodules using growth rate
criteria_or_scoring: Rapid VDT (<30 days) or very long VDT (>400 days) suggests benignity
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Malignant nodules tend to have irregular or spiculated edges; benign often have very short or very long VDT.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When serial scans are available to evaluate growth over time.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: rapid volume doubling time (<30 days) or a very long volume doubling time (>400 days) [5].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nodule margin characteristics classification (radiographic)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify nodule edge features associated with benign vs malignant etiologies
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Radiographic interpretation of pulmonary nodules.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Margin Smooth, well deﬁned Irregular, Lobulated Spiculated Sunburst or corona radiata appearance

diagnostic_approaches.name: Calcification pattern classification (radiographic)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Use intranodular calcification patterns to support benign vs malignant interpretation
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Radiographic interpretation of pulmonary nodules.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Calciﬁcation Central Diffuse solid Laminated Popcorn-like Diffuse and amorphous Punctate Eccentric

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nodule density classification: solid vs subsolid (including part-solid and ground glass)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify nodules by density to inform malignancy risk and growth patterns
criteria_or_scoring: Subsolid nodules (SSNs): part-solid and ground glass
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Descriptors considered separately due to differing prevalence of malignancy and growth patterns.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Radiographic characterization after nodule detection.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Nodules are divided into two categories, solid and subsolid, with subsolid nodules (SSNs) further classiﬁed into part-solid and ground glass.

diagnostic_approaches.name: FDG-PET or PET/CT for pulmonary nodule evaluation
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Functional imaging to evaluate IPNs and localize FDG uptake
criteria_or_scoring: Descriptive uptake categories: absent, mild, moderate, high
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Combination of CT and PET allows for functional and morphologic image capture and localization of FDG uptake.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Descriptive uptake (absent/mild/moderate/high) can aid risk stratification when integrated with clinical context.
limitations: False positives: pneumonia, granulomatous disease, sarcoidosis, amyloidosis, rounded atelectasis, pleural fibrosis
Posttreatment uptake: talc pleurodesis, radiation, chemotherapy, bone marrow stimulation
False negatives: lesions smaller than 1 cm; carcinoid, MIA, AIS; well-differentiated adenocarcinoma
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Most common functional test ordered for evaluation of an IPN; consider local endemic infection prevalence.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: showed a sensitivity of 89% and speciﬁcity of 75% for diagnosing lung cancer

diagnostic_approaches.name: Subsolid nodule (SSN) evaluation: TTNB and PET performance
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Highlight diagnostic performance of TTNB and PET in SSNs
criteria_or_scoring: Diagnostic yield of TTNB and PET metabolic activity is significantly lower in SSNs
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Lower diagnostic yield and metabolic activity in SSNs compared to solid nodules.
limitations: Significantly lower TTNB yield and PET activity in SSNs
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Caution when considering TTNB or PET for SSNs due to lower performance.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The diagnostic yield of transthoracic needle biopsy (TTNB) and metabolic activity on PET is signiﬁcantly lower in SSNs unless the solid component is larger than

diagnostic_approaches.name: Physician assessment of pretest probability of cancer (pCA)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Clinician-estimated pCA to distinguish benign vs malignant nodules
criteria_or_scoring: Based on nodule size, contour, and location
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Outperformed Mayo and VA models in distinguishing benign from malignant nodules in this cohort.
limitations: Management differed from guideline recommendations despite accurate predictions.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Pulmonary nodule or thoracic surgery clinics.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: in a population of 337 patients with a cancer prevalence of 47% [20].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Volumetric assessment: volume doubling time (VDT)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate benign versus malignant pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess nodule volume on serial CT scans and calculate volume doubling time
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Shorter VDT suggests malignancy; longer VDT suggests benign etiology
limitations: Assumes a nodule has an exponential growth rate
Volumetric measurements cannot accurately be performed in nonsolid or part-solid lesions
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: To assess changes between serial CT scans during surveillance
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Using a cutoff of 500 days, the specificity of this technique was 90%, sensitivity of 91%, NPV of 98%, and PPV of 67% [32].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Noncontrast low-dose chest CT for surveillance
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Surveillance imaging for pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Noncontrast low radiation dose chest CT
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Most patients undergoing surveillance
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Noncontrast low radiation dose chest CT should be used for most patients undergoing surveillance.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Blood-based rule-out biomarker (LG3BP and C163A + clinical risk factors)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Rule out malignancy in intermediate-risk pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Blood test measuring LG3BP and C163A combined with clinical risk factors
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: High NPV supports deferring invasive procedures in benign disease
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Intermediate risk pulmonary nodules 8–30 mm in size
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: demonstrated a sensitivity of 97%, specificity of 44%, and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 98% in patients presenting with intermediate risk pulmonary nodules 8–30 mm in size

diagnostic_approaches.name: Seven-autoantibody panel
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify malignant lung nodules (rule-in tendency)
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Intermediate risk nodules 4–20 mm in size
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: When applied to intermediate risk nodules 4–20 mm in size, a seven-autoantibody panel was shown to increase the risk of malignancy 2.7-fold [39].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nasal swab genomic classifier
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Evaluate probability of lung cancer in patients with IPNs
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Nasal swab to obtain nasal squamous epithelium for genomic classification
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Low-risk classifier functions as rule-out; high-risk classifier functions as rule-in
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Patients presenting with IPNs
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The low-risk classifier demonstrated a sensitivity of 96% and specificity of 42% to rule out lung cancer, while the high-risk classifier had a sensitivity of 58% and a specificity of 90% as a rule-in test [41].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) for mediastinal lymph nodes
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnostic evaluation of thoracic lymph nodes and lesions
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Highest diagnostic yield among compared bronchoscopic techniques
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: For mediastinal lymph nodes
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: EBUS (for mediastinal lymph nodes) had the highest diagnostic yield at 80%, which based on pCA prior to the procedure [44].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopy for peripheral IPNs (mixed modalities)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnostic evaluation of indeterminate peripheral pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Yield increased with higher pretest probability of cancer
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Evaluation of peripheral IPNs
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: EBUS, bronchoscopy with fluoroscopy, electromagnetic navigation (EMN), and combination bronchoscopy were compared, and overall diagnostic yield was 69% [44].

treatment_algorithms.title: American College of Chest Physicians 2013 Guidelines diagnostic algorithm
treatment_algorithms.source_excerpt: Fig. 1 American College of Chest Physicians 2013 Guidelines diagnostic algorithm. (Used with Permission from Gould et al. [14])

clinical_guidelines.title: American College of Chest Physicians Guidelines – Solid Nodules
specific_recommendations: Low-risk IPNs (pCA < 5%): manage with surveillance; for solid nodules <8 mm without risk factors, choose CT surveillance based on nodule size.
For solid nodules >8 mm with very low risk (<5% pCA): perform serial surveillance imaging at 3–6, 9–12, and 18–24 months.
If multiple nodules are present, base follow-up on the size of the largest nodule.
If a solid lesion is stable for 2 years, no further CT imaging is required.
Intermediate risk (pCA 5–65%): further evaluate with PET scan or nonsurgical biopsy (CT-guided or bronchoscopy depending on nodule factors).

If pretest probability is <30–40% and the lesion is not PET avid or is not more than 15 Hounsfield units, or if needle biopsy is nondiagnostic and the lesion is not PET avid, surveillance CT is advised.
High risk (pCA >65%): do not use functional imaging solely to characterize; pursue surgical diagnosis.
Consider nonsurgical biopsy before surgery if tumor mutational analysis is recommended (clinical stage 1B–3A).
Obtain PET imaging prior to treatment for lung cancer staging.
If lesion grows on surveillance, perform nonsurgical biopsy or surgical resection unless comorbidities make procedures high risk and SBRT is considered without tissue confirmation.
Consider surgical diagnosis if the nodule is PET avid or nonsurgical biopsy is suspicious for malignancy.
Use shared decision-making throughout care.

clinical_guidelines.title: American College of Chest Physicians Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules
clinical_guidelines.condition: Indeterminate pulmonary nodules (subsolid nodules, including pure ground glass and part-solid)
specific_recommendations: Pure ground glass nodule <5 mm: no further follow-up.
Pure ground glass nodule >5 mm: annual surveillance for at least 3 years.
Part solid defined as >50% ground glass.
Part-solid <8 mm: repeat CT at 3, 12, and 24 months, then annual scans for an additional 1–3 years.
Part-solid >8 mm: repeat CT in 3 months; if persistent and/or growing, evaluate with PET, biopsy, or resection.
Do not perform PET when the solid component is <8 mm.
Part-solid >15 mm: evaluate with PET, nonsurgical biopsy, or resection.

decision_points_and_pathways.pathway: No further follow-up
decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: pure ground glass nodule less than 5 mm in diameter, no further follow-up is recommended.

decision_points_and_pathways.pathway: Annual surveillance for at least 3 years
decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: If the lesion is more than 5 mm, annual surveillance is recommended for at least 3 years

decision_points_and_pathways.pathway: >50% ground glass
decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: Part solid is deﬁned as >50% ground glass.

decision_points_and_pathways.pathway: Do not perform PET scan
decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: PET scan should not be performed in those nodules with a solid component of less than 8 mm.

decision_points_and_pathways.pathway: Evaluate with PET, nonsurgical biopsy, or resection
decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: If the part-solid nodule is larger than 15 mm, further evaluation with PET, nonsurgical biopsy, or resection is warranted

contraindications_and_exceptions: Avoid PET when the solid component is <8 mm.

CT at 3, 12, 24 months then annual 1–3 years for part-solid <8 mm.
Repeat CT in 3 months for part-solid >8 mm before further evaluation.
alternative_approaches: Some guidelines recommend 5 years of surveillance for pure ground glass nodules.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In patients with a pure ground glass nodule less than 5 mm in diameter, no further follow-up is recommended.

clinical_guidelines.title: British Thoracic Society Guidelines – Indeterminate Pulmonary Nodule Assessment
specific_recommendations: Echo many ACCP recommendations.
Incorporate use of nodule calculators and volumetric measurements in initial assessment and follow-up.
Provide guidance on the use of image-guided biopsies.

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The British Thoracic Society (BTS) Guidelines echo many of the recommendations put forth in the ACCP guidelines.

clinical_guidelines.title: General approach to Subsolid Nodules (SSNs)
clinical_guidelines.condition: Subsolid pulmonary nodules (SSNs), including pure ground glass nodules
specific_recommendations: Risk depends on size and growth of the solid component; larger solid component increases malignancy risk.
Generally manage SSNs with surveillance unless the solid component is growing.
When the solid component grows, recommend biopsy of the solid component or surgical resection.
Diagnostic yield of TTNB and PET is significantly lower in SSNs unless the solid component is >8 mm.
Pure ground glass nodules are often biologically indolent; in most cases, surveillance is recommended.

monitoring_requirements: Surveillance for SSNs unless the solid component is growing.
outcome_measures: 100% 5-year survival for malignant pure GGNs in a resected series.

technology_and_technique.topic: Subsolid nodules: impact on TTNB and PET
technology_and_technique.summary: For subsolid nodules (SSNs), both transthoracic needle biopsy (TTNB) diagnostic yield and PET metabolic activity are significantly lower; performance improves when the solid component is larger or increasing even if overall size is stable. Exact yield percentages not provided in the excerpt.

technology_and_technique.topic: Size-based malignancy risk for patient selection
technology_and_technique.summary: Malignancy probability is ~1% for nodules <6 mm and ~1–2% for 6–8 mm, supporting surveillance rather than invasive biopsy for many small nodules.

Benign nodules: smaller, smooth, VDT <30 days or >400 days. Malignant nodules: larger, irregular/spiculated, VDT 30–500 days. These features inform selection for invasive diagnostics versus surveillance.

technology_and_technique.topic: Pretest probability models to guide modality choice
technology_and_technique.summary: Mayo, Herder, Brock, and TREAT models estimate pretest probability of cancer (pCA) to triage patients to surveillance, additional functional imaging, or invasive biopsy/surgery; used to balance diagnostic yield against procedural risk.

ACCP and BTS guidelines incorporate pCA to select surveillance, PET/CT, or tissue diagnosis (e.g., TTNB or surgery). Comparative effectiveness data and specific yields are not detailed in the excerpt.
technology_and_technique.reference: ACCP Guidelines; BTS Guidelines (Chapter text Sections 4.1–4.2)
